requirement_text.REQ-386: Time-limited, expiring signed URLs for instance-attachment byte content, replacing direct unbounded authenticated GET. Filed from the GUI-review UAT run of test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/attachment-cross-tenant-probe.yaml (PW-09) -- see test/uat-reports/gui-review-2026-09-20-attachment-cross-tenant-probe.md. First of three requirements from that finding (REQ-387 frontend, blocked on this one; REQ-388 audit logging, independent). WHAT EXISTS TODAY (confirmed by reading current source): REQ-211/212 (both done) built a fully working, tenant-isolated attachment store -- Letflow.Repository.Attachments.upload/2, list/2, get/2, delete/2, and GET/POST/DELETE /instances/:id/attachments[/:id] routes in lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex. Cross-tenant, cross-instance-same-tenant, malformed/never-issued-UUID, and genuinely-nonexistent-id all fold to the same {:error, :not_found} tuple in fetch_scoped_attachment_content/3 (around line 1156), rendered via the same Response.not_found(conn) call -- EO-001/EO-002 satisfied today at the API layer. WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: handle_get_attachment_content/3 serves raw byte content directly from a normal authenticated GET with no time bound at all -- no signed-URL concept anywhere in the codebase. THIS REQUIREMENT builds that mechanism, backend only: (1) a new endpoint (e.g. POST /instances/:id/attachments/:attachment_id/link), same :AttachmentsRead permission as the existing content route, issues a signed, time-limited token (HMAC over attachment_id + expiry timestamp + a server-held secret, or Phoenix.Token-style if already in use -- check before inventing a second signing scheme) and returns a URL/token plus its expiry. Choose and state a concrete, short expiry (minutes, not hours -- name the exact value and rationale in the design doc, flag for REVIEWER same as REQ-211's @max_upload_bytes precedent). (2) the existing content-serving route (or a new one keyed by the signed token instead of a bare id) verifies the token's signature and expiry before calling Attachments.get_content/2 -- an expired or invalid token returns a plain, explicit 'link expired, request a new one' response (EO-003) and never serves content, with no distinguishable difference between 'expired' and 'tampered/invalid' beyond what's needed for EO-003's own message -- must not reopen the existence-probing gap REQ-211/212 closed: an expired-token response for a foreign tenant's attachment id must remain indistinguishable from one for a never-issued id (EO-001). (3) requesting a fresh link for the same attachment after a prior one expired succeeds normally and serves the document (EO-004). OUT OF SCOPE: frontend document-viewer screen (REQ-387); any change to REQ-211/212's existing tenant/instance-scoping logic (must not weaken it); audit logging of denied attempts (REQ-388).
